suggestions.reason: The clause references "the services described in this Agreement" without establishing a defined term or anchoring that description to a specific exhibit, schedule, or statement of work, leaving the precise scope of Consultant's obligations open to dispute—a direct risk to Columbia Capital Management if the counterparty later contests the boundaries of what was engaged. Additionally, the clause records Consultant's acceptance of the engagement but states no corresponding obligation on the City's part, meaning Columbia Capital Management's entitlement to compensation for performing those services rests entirely on other provisions that may not be clearly cross-referenced back to this operative engagement clause. If those fee provisions are ambiguous or omitted, Columbia Capital Management has no express contractual hook within the engagement itself to enforce payment.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement and Consultant accepts that engagement.

suggestions.reason: The clause references Exhibit A for the description of Contract Services but does not state that Exhibit A constitutes the complete and exclusive scope, nor does it expressly identify what falls outside the scope, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to scope creep claims by the City. Without an explicit out-of-scope boundary, the City could argue that additional work is encompassed within the existing Contract Services, depriving Columbia Capital Management of its right to additional compensation or a signed amendment. The existing amendment requirement protects Columbia Capital Management in principle, but its effectiveness is undermined if the original scope is not precisely bounded, since a disputed boundary can defeat the threshold question of whether a change order is required at all.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement, incorporated herein by reference, and which constitutes the complete and exclusive description of the Contract Services. Any services not expressly described in Exhibit A are outside the scope of this Agreement. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, and Consultant shall not be obligated to commence any additional services, except on the basis of a written supplemental agreement or amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no operative payment terms whatsoever, deferring entirely to Exhibit A without specifying the fee structure, invoicing process, payment due date, expense treatment, or any right to dispute an invoice — leaving Columbia Capital Management, as the Consultant, exposed to indefinite payment delays and without any contractual mechanism to enforce timely receipt of fees. If Exhibit A is incomplete or silent on any of these elements, Columbia Capital Management has no enforceable payment right beyond a bare obligation to pay an unspecified amount at an unspecified time. The absence of a dispute procedure and late payment consequence further means that if the City withholds or delays payment, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual leverage or accruing remedy. Exhibit A must be fully completed to give this clause operative effect, and the survival and termination provisions should be reviewed to confirm that payment obligations for pre-termination Contract Services survive expiry or early termination.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As presently drafted, the clause permits the City to terminate this Agreement for cause without affording Columbia Capital Management any opportunity to cure an alleged breach, meaning a disputed or minor performance issue could be weaponized to strip Columbia Capital Management of an ongoing engagement and future fees without warning or recourse. The absence of a cure period is particularly prejudicial to Columbia Capital Management because it removes a standard contractual protection and leaves the definition of "cause" entirely at the City's unilateral discretion. Additionally, the clause does not specify when termination takes effect upon the expiry of the notice period, creating ambiguity over Columbia Capital Management's entitlement to fees and expenses in the intervening period. The survival provision covers indemnity and insurance but should be read alongside the payment obligations to confirm that Columbia Capital Management's right to fees for pre-termination Contract Services also survives.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Consultant, or for cause upon written notice specifying the material breach alleged, provided that Consultant shall have thirty (30) days following receipt of such notice to cure the stated breach before termination takes effect. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the effective date of termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the effective date of termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the Agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' written notice, effective upon expiration of such notice period. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the Compliance with Laws clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to material legal and reputational risk by omitting three market-standard protections: an express anti-bribery and anti-corruption obligation on the Consultant, a notification requirement compelling the Consultant to disclose any known legal violation affecting the Contract Services or this Agreement, and any supply-chain labor standard addressing forced labor, child labor, or human trafficking. Without these requirements, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual trigger to learn of a compliance failure before it ripens into a legal or reputational liability, and no express basis to insist on anti-corruption and supply-chain due-diligence conduct by the Consultant. The existing indemnification in favor of the City is undermined if the predicate compliance obligations are insufficiently defined.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted binds Consultant only to two Kansas-specific anti-discrimination statutes, leaving Columbia Capital Management entirely unprotected against bribery and corruption exposure, undisclosed legal breaches by Consultant that could taint the engagement, and supply-chain risks involving forced or child labour — all of which can generate direct regulatory and reputational liability for Columbia Capital Management. The absence of a breach-notification obligation is particularly harmful to Columbia Capital Management because it may remain unaware of a Consultant violation until after damage has occurred, foreclosing timely remedial action. The clause should be expanded surgically to close these gaps without restructuring the existing anti-discrimination core.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant shall comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.), the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.), and all other applicable laws and regulations, including applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and supply-chain labour standards prohibiting forced and child labour, and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Consultant shall promptly notify Columbia Capital Management in writing of any breach of applicable law or regulation that affects performance under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The insurance obligation currently runs only "throughout the duration of this Agreement," leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to uninsured losses arising from pre-termination work where claims surface after the Agreement ends—a material risk in a professional services context where errors, omissions, or other latent deficiencies may not manifest until well after Consultant's engagement concludes. Without a post-term tail requirement, Consultant could allow coverage to lapse on the day the Agreement expires, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no insured counterparty for retrospective claims. Additionally, the clause contains no statement that the procurement of insurance is a floor, not a ceiling, on Consultant's liability; absent such language, Consultant may contend that policy limits represent the outer boundary of its financial exposure to Columbia Capital Management, undermining any broader liability or indemnification regime elsewhere in the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of three (3) years following expiration or termination of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The procurement and maintenance of such insurance shall not be construed to limit or otherwise affect Consultant's liability to The City under this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 9 imposes a broad, uncapped indemnification obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management (as Consultant) with no reciprocal protection, leaving Columbia Capital Management fully exposed to claims arising from the City's own negligent or intentional acts. The clause also strips Columbia Capital Management of any right to control the defense of covered claims or withhold consent to settlement, which could result in Columbia Capital Management being bound by adverse dispositions it had no power to prevent. The absence of any cross-reference to the Agreement's liability limitations means this indemnity could operate as an unlimited backstop, overriding any cap that otherwise applies to Columbia Capital Management's exposure. Additionally, there is no mitigation obligation on the City, allowing it to allow losses to accumulate at Columbia Capital Management's expense.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, and subject to any limitation of liability set forth in this Agreement, (a) Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services; and (b) the City shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Consultant and its officers, employees, and agents from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the City or its elected officials, officers, employees, or agents. The indemnifying party shall have the right to control the defense of any covered claim and shall not be bound by any settlement entered into without its prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld. Each party shall give the other prompt written notice of any claim, suit, or demand subject to this provision, shall reasonably cooperate in the defense thereof, and shall take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate its losses.

suggestions.reason: The clause restricts third-party suits only as to "personal injuries or property damage," leaving unaddressed a broad range of claims that third parties could assert against Columbia Capital Management as a professional services consultant — including economic loss, professional liability, and financial harm claims arising from this Agreement. That narrow enumeration creates a material enforcement gap: a court could read the clause as impliedly permitting third-party suits based on categories of harm not listed, exposing Columbia Capital Management to litigation it reasonably expected this provision to foreclose. Additionally, the unqualified reservation that duties "shall remain as imposed by law" functions as an open-ended carve-out that could allow third parties to invoke statutory or regulatory duties owed to them, effectively undermining the entire no-third-party-beneficiary protection for Columbia Capital Management without any agreed limitation or reciprocal benefit.
suggestions.original_text: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for any claims or damages of any kind arising out of or relating to this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law, except that neither party shall be liable to any third party for claims arising solely from the terms or provisions of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to substantial legal and financial risk on multiple fronts. The unilateral forum provision — permitting whichever party initiates a claim to pursue "such steps as it deems necessary" — means the City could drag Columbia Capital Management into any forum of the City's choosing without limitation, creating unpredictable litigation costs and jurisdictional exposure. The absence of governing law compounds this uncertainty, leaving Columbia Capital Management without a stable legal framework to assess its rights and obligations. Most critically, the continue-performance obligation is entirely one-sided: Columbia Capital Management must keep delivering services during a dispute, yet the clause imposes no corresponding obligation on the City to continue making payments, leaving Columbia Capital Management performing without remedy. No provision preserves Columbia Capital Management's right to seek urgent injunctive or equitable relief, which is a material gap if, for example, the City misappropriates Columbia Capital Management's proprietary work product during a live dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.

suggestions.reason: The existing Representations clause contains only a narrow anti-collusion pricing statement, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no contractual assurance that the Services will be performed to any defined standard of skill or care, no protection against third-party intellectual property infringement arising from the Services, no defined remedy if a warranty is breached, and no warranty period during which Columbia Capital Management may assert a claim. In practical terms, this exposes Columbia Capital Management to receiving substandard or infringing work with no express contractual basis to demand correction, re-performance, or a refund, and no defined window within which to raise such a claim.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. Provider further warrants that the Services shall be performed with reasonable skill and care, shall not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights, and that in the event of any breach of these warranties, Provider shall, at Columbia Capital Management's election, re-perform the non-conforming Services or refund the fees paid therefor; such warranties shall apply for one (1) year following completion of the applicable Services.

suggestions.reason: The representations clause as drafted is narrowly confined to the City's anti-gratuity and kickback policy, providing Columbia Capital Management with no contractual warranty that the Consultant will comply with applicable laws and regulations in the performance of its services. Without a general legal compliance representation, Columbia Capital Management has no clear contractual basis to treat the Consultant's violation of employment, securities, data protection, or other applicable laws as a breach giving rise to remedies or termination for cause. This gap is particularly material for Columbia Capital Management given the regulated financial services environment in which it operates. The word "promises" should also be replaced with the operative modal "shall not" to impose a proper contractual obligation rather than an informal commitment.
suggestions.original_text: The Consultant has not violated, is not violating, and promises that it will not violate the City’s policy of prohibition against gratuities and kickbacks.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The Consultant has not violated, is not violating, and shall not violate any applicable law or regulation, including the City's policy of prohibition against gratuities and kickbacks.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the authority representation runs only in one direction: the Consultant warrants its capacity to execute and perform the Agreement, but Columbia Capital Management makes no equivalent representation. This asymmetry creates an enforceability risk for Columbia Capital Management — if the Consultant were to later contest whether Columbia Capital Management had authority to bind itself, the Agreement provides no corresponding warranty to rebut that challenge. Mutual authority representations are market-standard in professional services agreements and their absence leaves Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce the Agreement's rights and obligations exposed to procedural attack.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The warranty standards in this clause — "recognized professional standards prevalent in their field," "state of the art procedures and techniques," and "ready comprehension of the required subject matter" — are legally indeterminate, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no objective benchmark against which to measure or enforce the Consultant's performance. If the Consultant delivers substandard work and Columbia Capital Management seeks to invoke these warranties, a dispute over what any of these phrases actually required would almost certainly require costly extrinsic evidence, substantially weakening Columbia Capital Management's enforcement position. Additionally, the clause imposes substantive warranty obligations on the Consultant but grants Columbia Capital Management no express remedy — such as a right to require re-performance — if those obligations are breached, creating an asymmetry that leaves Columbia Capital Management dependent on general common law remedies that may be uncertain or limited in scope. Anchoring the standard to applicable professional or industry bodies and adding a targeted re-performance remedy closes both gaps without materially altering the clause's structure.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform to or exceed the professional standards generally recognized by applicable professional or industry bodies for services of the type provided hereunder. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with professional expertise, skills, and knowledge consistent with current practices and techniques applicable to all relevant subject matters. The Consultant shall be capable of performing the consulting and other services required herein and shall possess the requisite expertise to provide such services. If any work or services fail to conform to these warranties, Columbia Capital Management may require the Consultant to re-perform such non-conforming work promptly and at no additional cost to Columbia Capital Management.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 14 imposes an assignment restriction solely on Consultant, granting the City unfettered, unilateral consent rights with no standard of reasonableness and no response deadline — exposing Columbia Capital Management to indefinite delay or arbitrary refusal when it seeks to reorganize, bring in an affiliate, or complete a corporate transaction. The provision is entirely silent on the City's own assignment rights, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no reciprocal protection against the City transferring its obligations to a less creditworthy or operationally suitable successor. Additionally, the clause contains no continuing-liability obligation on the assigning party and no notice requirement upon a permitted transfer, further undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to manage its counterparty exposure through any change of control event.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, except that either party may assign to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, in each case upon written notice to the other party. The assigning party shall remain liable for its obligations hereunder unless expressly released in writing. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the permitted successors and assigns of the parties.

suggestions.reason: The notices block sets out Columbia Capital Management's contact details but contains no mechanism by which either party may update those details over time. Without such a mechanism, a counterparty could argue that notice sent to a stale or superseded address remains legally effective, exposing Columbia Capital Management to the risk of missing time-sensitive communications—such as breach notices, termination notices, or indemnity claims—that trigger response obligations or cure periods elsewhere in the Agreement. A brief change-of-notice provision eliminates this ambiguity and preserves Columbia Capital Management's ability to redirect formal communications without dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may change its notice details by providing the other party with at least ten (10) days' prior written notice of such change.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three material gaps that undermine the independent contractor classification it depends upon. First, the absence of any control-of-means language leaves open the possibility that the City could assert supervisory authority over how Columbia Capital Management performs its services, which is a primary factor courts examine when reclassifying contractors as employees and would expose Columbia Capital Management to retroactive employment-related liabilities. Second, the taxes and withholdings obligation is unilaterally imposed on Consultant only, with no corresponding language requiring the City to bear the costs, taxes, and benefits of its own personnel, creating an asymmetric allocation of personnel-related financial risk. Third, the omission of a mutual non-authority-to-bind provision means Columbia Capital Management has no express contractual shield against the City purporting to act as its agent or bind it to third-party commitments, a risk that is particularly acute for a capital management firm given the financial and regulatory consequences of unauthorized commitments.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor who shall control the manner and means of performing the services hereunder. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Each party shall be solely responsible for all costs, taxes, withholdings, and benefits of its own personnel. Neither party shall have authority to bind the other to any obligation or commitment. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to several material gaps: it imposes no anti-bribery, anti-corruption, or supply-chain labor compliance obligations on either party, creates no mechanism by which Columbia Capital Management would be notified if the City breaches a law materially affecting this Agreement, and allocates the entire cost of any change-in-law compliance burden to Columbia Capital Management without recourse. Most critically for Columbia Capital Management, the City's unfettered "sole discretion" non-appropriation right relieves all obligations "without penalty," meaning Columbia Capital Management could have rendered Services and incurred costs in a renewal term only to receive no payment whatsoever if the City simply declines to budget funds, with no preserved right to recover for work already performed.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended, and all other applicable laws and regulations, including those governing anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and applicable labor and supply-chain standards prohibiting forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing of any breach of applicable law that materially affects this Agreement, and any increase in the cost of performance caused by a change in applicable law shall be addressed by written amendment to this Agreement. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all ongoing obligations under this Agreement without penalty; provided that the City shall remain obligated to pay Columbia Capital Management for all Services rendered and expenses incurred prior to the effective date of non-appropriation. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

suggestions.reason: The term "legal actions" is undefined in the Agreement, creating a material ambiguity about whether the exclusive venue clause captures arbitration proceedings, equitable relief actions, or regulatory enforcement matters—all of which are commercially significant to Columbia Capital Management as a capital management firm. More critically, the clause designates only a Kansas state court, with no carve-out for federal jurisdiction; if federal securities, investment adviser, or other statutory claims arise, a counterparty could argue that Columbia Capital Management filed in the wrong forum, exposing it to dismissal, delay, and unnecessary litigation expense. Replacing "legal actions" with the broader phrase "disputes or claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement" and expressly preserving access to the federal District of Kansas for federal law claims eliminates both ambiguities while keeping the venue framework substantively intact.
suggestions.original_text: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions arising out of this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any disputes or claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas, or the United States District Court for the District of Kansas for any claims arising under federal law.

suggestions.reason: The current provision does nothing more than designate Kansas law; it omits a forum, pre-dispute escalation steps, mutual venue binding, an injunctive-relief carve-out, and a continued-performance obligation. For Columbia Capital Management, this means that if a dispute arises—over fees, deliverables, or confidentiality—there is no agreed mechanism to resolve it short of full litigation, no court with certain jurisdiction, and no assurance that the counterparty will not cease performing or seek relief in an inconvenient forum. The absence of a continued-performance obligation is particularly prejudicial to Columbia Capital Management, as it could allow the counterparty to withhold Services mid-engagement the moment a dispute is raised.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.

suggestions.reason: The second sentence of Section 21 states that "use of or failure to use capitals shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation" of any term, but this sweeping formulation creates an interpretive risk for Columbia Capital Management because the Agreement's definitional scheme almost certainly relies on capitalized Defined Terms to carry their assigned meanings. If a counterparty or court reads this provision literally, it could argue that capitalised terms such as "Services," "Confidential Information," or "Agreement" need not be construed according to their stated definitions, potentially exposing Columbia Capital Management to broader obligations or narrower rights than the parties intended. A surgical carve-out preserving the operative effect of expressly defined terms eliminates this ambiguity without otherwise disturbing the clause.
suggestions.original_text: Section 21. Descriptive Headings and Capitalization. The descriptive headings of the provisions of this Agreement are formulated and used only for convenience and shall not be deemed to affect the meaning and construction of any such provision. Some terms are capitalized throughout the Agreement, but use of or failure to use capitals shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation of such terms.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 21. Descriptive Headings and Capitalization. The descriptive headings of the provisions of this Agreement are formulated and used only for convenience and shall not be deemed to affect the meaning and construction of any such provision. Some terms are capitalized throughout the Agreement; provided, however, that where a term is expressly defined herein, the capitalized form of such term shall be construed in accordance with its stated definition, and inconsistent capitalization of any term that is not expressly defined shall have no legal bearing on the interpretation of such term.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is commercially ambiguous: it does not identify by what standard, by whose determination, or to what extent the reformation occurs, meaning a counterparty could argue that an invalid provision has been automatically reformed in a manner favorable to itself and adverse to Columbia Capital Management without any court supervision or regard for the parties' original intent. Without an objective benchmark anchoring the reformation — such as preserving the parties' original intent to the greatest extent possible — Columbia Capital Management faces the practical risk that a broad or burdensome provision adjudicated invalid could be rewritten by operation of this clause in a way that imposes a modified but still disadvantageous obligation on Columbia Capital Management. The addition of a minimum-extent and intent-preservation standard resolves this ambiguity and provides an objective benchmark that a court could apply without resort to extrinsic evidence.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall be reformed and amended to the minimum extent necessary to make such provision valid and enforceable while preserving the original intent of the parties as closely as possible, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: The clause addresses non-waiver by inaction and requires written, signed waivers, but it omits the standard protection that a waiver of one specific breach or right does not constitute a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or right. Without this language, a counterparty could argue that Columbia Capital Management's express written waiver of a particular breach establishes a pattern or precedent that weakens Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce other or later obligations under the Agreement. This gap creates a material enforcement risk for Columbia Capital Management, particularly where repeated or similar counterparty defaults may arise across the term of the engagement.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party. No waiver of any particular breach or right shall be construed as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or right, whether of the same or of a different nature.

suggestions.reason: The reference to "documents incorporated by reference" is undefined and unspecified, creating a material risk for Columbia Capital Management: a counterparty could assert that any number of pre-contractual documents—proposals, pitch decks, or email exchanges—qualify as "incorporated by reference," thereby expanding or varying Columbia Capital Management's obligations beyond what was expressly agreed. Additionally, limiting the integration clause to "the professional services set forth herein" rather than the full subject matter of the Agreement introduces a potential gap, leaving open the possibility that a court could admit extrinsic evidence on collateral matters that Columbia Capital Management reasonably understood to be governed exclusively by the written Agreement. These ambiguities could undermine Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce the Agreement as written and resist claims grounded in pre-contractual communications.
suggestions.original_text: Section 24. Merger. This Agreement and the documents incorporated by reference constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the professional services set forth herein. There are no verbal understandings, agreements, representations or warranties between the parties that are not expressly set forth herein. This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties, both written and oral.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 24. Merger. This Agreement and any schedules, exhibits, and statements of work attached hereto or expressly identified herein as incorporated by reference constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof. There are no verbal understandings, agreements, representations or warranties between the parties that are not expressly set forth herein. This Agreement supersedes all prior agreements and understandings between the parties, both written and oral.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 25 protects only the City by providing that verbal statements of City officials or representatives cannot alter or form part of this Agreement; it imposes no equivalent restriction on verbal statements made by Columbia Capital Management's own officials or representatives. This one-sided drafting means that verbal statements attributable to Columbia Capital Management's personnel could potentially be argued by the City to constitute binding modifications or admissions, while the City enjoys complete insulation from any such exposure. Left unaddressed, this asymmetry creates meaningful legal and financial risk for Columbia Capital Management, as the City could selectively invoke verbal communications made by Columbia Capital Management's representatives while remaining wholly shielded from its own. The provision should be made mutual so that neither party is bound by the verbal statements of its officials or representatives.
suggestions.original_text: Section 25. Verbal Statements Not Binding. It is understood and agreed that the written terms and provisions of this Agreement supersede all verbal statements of any and every official or other representative of the City, and such statements shall not be effective or be construed as entering into, or forming a part of, or altering in any way whatsoever, this written Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 25. Verbal Statements Not Binding. It is understood and agreed that the written terms and provisions of this Agreement supersede all verbal statements of any and every official or other representative of either party, and such statements shall not be effective or be construed as entering into, or forming a part of, or altering in any way whatsoever, this written Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The current clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three material risks: it fails to require a signature by an authorized representative of each party, meaning a counterparty could assert that an amendment was validly executed by any employee; it does not expressly cover schedules and exhibits, leaving ancillary documents potentially modifiable outside the written-amendment requirement; and it contains no express prohibition on oral modifications or modification by conduct, which creates a risk that email exchanges, verbal commitments, or course of dealing could be argued to alter Columbia Capital Management's rights and obligations under this Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including all schedules and exhibits hereto, may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by an authorized representative of each party. No oral agreement, course of dealing, or conduct shall operate to amend or modify this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, the survivorship clause expressly identifies only Consultant's obligations—Insurance and Indemnification—leaving Columbia Capital Management's most critical post-termination protections, such as confidentiality, intellectual property ownership, and accrued payment rights, to rest solely on the vague catch-all phrase "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination," which a court or arbitrator could resolve against Columbia Capital Management. The uncertainty created by that phrase means Columbia Capital Management could face a credible argument that its key rights simply lapsed upon termination, exposing the firm to unauthorized use of proprietary information and unenforceable IP claims after the engagement ends. The one-sided structure of the clause—naming only the Consultant's obligations without expressly preserving Columbia Capital Management's corresponding rights—further reinforces that imbalance. Replacing "should survive" with "survive by their nature" and expressly enumerating Columbia Capital Management's core protections eliminates the interpretive gap.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), Columbia Capital Management's rights with respect to Confidentiality and Intellectual Property, and any other terms and conditions that by their nature survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" imposes an unbounded compliance obligation on Columbia Capital Management with no defined scope, meaning any law, regulation, or legal requirement that any party later asserts to be "applicable" could be used to establish a breach and trigger unlimited liability exposure. The clause simultaneously places all operative obligations exclusively on Columbia Capital Management while imposing no corresponding duty on the City — for example, no obligation to provide timely, accurate information necessary for Columbia Capital Management to manage the Accounts — creating a commercially unjustified asymmetry. Left unaddressed, this combination of vague legal compliance language and unilateral obligation structure materially increases Columbia Capital Management's litigation exposure and forecloses defenses grounded in the City's own cooperation failures.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing the provision of investment advisory services. The City shall provide Consultant with timely access to all information and documentation reasonably necessary to enable Consultant to fulfill its responsibilities under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "an enterprise of like character and with like aims" is undefined nowhere in this Agreement, which creates a material enforcement risk for Columbia Capital Management: a Consultant facing a breach claim could argue that the relevant comparator enterprise operates at a lower standard or in a different market segment, effectively diluting the fiduciary duty Columbia Capital Management bargained for. Because the standard for measuring the Consultant's conduct is left to extrinsic interpretation, any dispute over whether the Consultant discharged its fiduciary obligations becomes a contested battle of expert evidence rather than an objectively determinable contractual benchmark. The clause also provides no express right for Columbia Capital Management to rely on or enforce the standard — it imposes the duty without anchoring it to the specific nature of the investment management services being provided under this Agreement. Anchoring the standard to the Consultant's specific professional capacity as an investment adviser managing discretionary assets eliminates that definitional ambiguity and gives Columbia Capital Management a clear, objective benchmark against which to measure the Consultant's conduct.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent investment adviser acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in managing discretionary investment assets of a similar type and scale on behalf of institutional clients.

suggestions.reason: The clause requires Columbia Capital Management to manage subportfolios against each subportfolio's "unique needs" and "statutory constraints" without defining or referencing where those needs and constraints are established, and to maintain "adequate liquidity" without any objective benchmark. This creates material exposure for Columbia Capital Management: the City could later assert that the investment strategy failed to reflect undocumented or unilaterally determined needs, or that Columbia Capital Management violated statutory constraints that were never formally communicated, potentially triggering liability under the Agreement's breach and indemnification provisions. Without written anchors for these standards, Columbia Capital Management has no objective basis to demonstrate compliance or contest a disputed claim.
suggestions.original_text: Implementing an investment strategy that allocates the City’s pooled cash into multiple subportfolios with the investments in each subportfolio targeted to the unique needs for and statutory constraints on those subportfolios. Subordinate to the core investment goals of preserving principal and providing adequate liquidity, Consultant shall seek to maximize income from the portfolio that the City can use to support its operations.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Implementing an investment strategy that allocates the City's pooled cash into multiple subportfolios, with the investments in each subportfolio targeted to the investment objectives and needs specified in writing by the City and the applicable statutory constraints identified in writing by the City for those subportfolios. Subordinate to the core investment goals of preserving principal and providing adequate liquidity in accordance with the City's written liquidity requirements, Consultant shall seek to maximize income from the portfolio that the City can use to support its operations.

suggestions.reason: The term "periodic" is undefined and sets no fixed reporting schedule, exposing Columbia Capital Management to an open-ended obligation under which the City could demand reporting at any frequency it chooses, creating an unpredictable operational burden and potential breach exposure if Columbia Capital Management's internal reporting cadence is later deemed insufficient. Without a defined trigger or schedule, Columbia Capital Management also has no objective standard against which to measure compliance, leaving the obligation unenforceable in its favor if a dispute arises. Anchoring the reporting obligation to a defined calendar frequency eliminates this ambiguity and gives Columbia Capital Management a clear, measurable standard of performance.
suggestions.original_text: Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Providing quarterly portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to significant legal and financial risk by allowing the City to unilaterally alter investment policy objectives and guidelines "from time to time" with no advance notice requirement, no transition period, and no protection for investment decisions already made in compliance with the guidelines then in effect. This creates an irreconcilable internal tension: Columbia Capital Management is granted "sole discretion" on one hand, yet is simultaneously bound by guidelines that the City may change without warning, meaning Columbia Capital Management could be held in breach for investments that were compliant when made. Without a minimum notice period before amended guidelines take effect, Columbia Capital Management bears unlimited exposure for policy changes it had no meaningful opportunity to act upon. A cross-reference review should confirm that any liability limitation provision elsewhere in the Agreement expressly covers investment decisions made in conformity with the City's written guidelines as then in effect.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City upon reasonable prior written notice, and no amendment or modification to such written investment policy objectives and guidelines shall be binding on Consultant until at least ten (10) Business Days following Consultant's receipt of written notice of such change. Consultant shall not be liable for investment decisions made in conformity with the written investment policy objectives and guidelines then in effect at the time of such decision. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" imposes no objectively enforceable standard on the City, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no reliable basis to demand, or enforce, the receipt of account balances and statements needed to manage the City's investment portfolio. Without a fixed delivery deadline, delays in receiving this financial data could impair Columbia Capital Management's ability to execute the investment plan and expose it to liability for investment decisions made on stale or incomplete information. A court asked to enforce this obligation would be forced to resort to extrinsic evidence to determine what "timely" means, making the provision practically unenforceable from Columbia Capital Management's perspective.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts no later than five (5) Business Days following the close of each calendar month.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the obligation is triggered "upon request" with no specification of the form that request must take or any timeframe within which the City must respond, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no enforceable mechanism to compel timely delivery of the historical account balances and cash flows it requires to perform its core liquidity-determination function. In practice, the City could acknowledge a request but defer compliance indefinitely without being in breach, directly impairing Columbia Capital Management's ability to execute the investment mandate. Without a defined response timeline, Columbia Capital Management bears the operational and reputational risk of liquidity miscalculation caused entirely by the City's inaction.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon written request by Consultant, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows promptly following such request, and in any event within five (5) Business Days, to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "as necessary to effect the investment plan" leaves "investment plan" undefined within the clause and, based on the evidence, the broader Agreement, exposing Columbia Capital Management to a scenario where the City disputes whether a particular transfer falls within the scope of its cooperation obligation, thereby blocking transactions Columbia Capital Management needs to perform its mandate. More critically, the clause imposes the obligation on the City without granting Columbia Capital Management any corresponding remedy or protection: if the City delays or fails to respond to a wire transfer request, Columbia Capital Management faces the risk of being treated as having failed to execute the investment strategy, with no express contractual shield against that characterization. Adding a clear qualifier to "investment plan" and a performance-fault carve-out directly protects Columbia Capital Management from liability arising from the City's own non-cooperation.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with reasonable notice, the City shall respond to Consultant's requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts as necessary to effect the then-current investment plan, provided that the City's failure or delay in responding shall not constitute or be attributed to a default by Consultant.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes no deadline on the City to instruct the Custodian following receipt of Consultant's confirmation, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to settlement failure risk if the City delays acting on trade instructions without consequence. The phrase "copies of confirmations" is undefined and insufficiently described, enabling the City or Custodian to dispute whether a given communication constitutes a qualifying confirmation, which could stall settlement and generate failed-trade liability against Columbia Capital Management. The absence of a defined confirmation standard also leaves Columbia Capital Management without a clear mechanism to establish that it has discharged its instruction obligations, undermining its ability to enforce the clause or defend against settlement-related claims.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1), the City shall instruct the Custodian, within one (1) Business Day following receipt of a written trade confirmation from Consultant, to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with such written trade confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains no obligation requiring Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to Columbia Capital Management, leaving the City entirely dependent on Consultant's self-policing with no independent right to be informed when a conflict arises. The conflict-avoidance mechanism is framed as Consultant's unilateral internal "policy" rather than a binding contractual obligation, meaning Consultant could modify or depart from that policy without breaching the Agreement. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates direct financial exposure: undisclosed conflicts could result in investment opportunities being withheld or misallocated without the City's knowledge or consent, and the existing language effectively insulates Consultant from liability for those outcomes by characterizing investment limitations as an acceptable by-product of the policy. The absence of any prescribed consequence when a conflict materially impairs the City's investment opportunities further leaves Columbia Capital Management without a meaningful remedy.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

suggestions.reason: The City's unilateral right to amend Schedule X "at any time" with nothing more than unspecified "notice provided to Consultant" creates material operational and legal exposure for Columbia Capital Management: without a defined minimum advance-notice period, the City could substitute or revoke an authorized individual's authority instantaneously, leaving Columbia Capital Management without adequate time to verify credentials, update internal controls, or reject instructions already acted upon in good faith. This unilateral, unchecked amendment right, coupled with the absence of any requirement that amendments take effect only upon actual receipt of notice, means Columbia Capital Management could face liability for acting on instructions from an individual whose authority was silently revoked. Additionally, "Schedule X" is an unfilled placeholder that must be completed before execution, as reliance on a non-existent or mis-identified schedule renders the authorized-persons framework unenforceable and exposes Columbia Capital Management to disputes about whose directions it was obligated to follow.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.

suggestions.reason: The Management Fees clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to significant financial and operational risk by omitting several material payment terms: the clause does not specify when invoices are issued, when payment falls due, or what rights Columbia Capital Management has to dispute a fee calculation it believes is erroneous — leaving Columbia Capital Management with no contractual basis to withhold a disputed amount without risking a claimed default. Additionally, the clause contains no mechanism requiring advance notice before the fee rate is changed, meaning Consultant could unilaterally alter the economic terms of the engagement, and the "sole compensation" language does not expressly confirm that expenses are included, leaving that point open to dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Invoices shall be issued within fifteen (15) days following each quarter-end, and payment shall be due within thirty (30) days of receipt of each invoice. Columbia Capital Management may dispute any invoice in writing within such thirty (30)-day period, and disputed amounts shall be withheld pending resolution without constituting a default. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. The fee rate may not be changed without at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice to Columbia Capital Management. Such amount, inclusive of all expenses related to investment advisory services, shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes a written notice obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management as Consultant, requiring it to notify the City of events pertaining to the Accounts and/or Consultant, but creates no corresponding obligation on the City to notify Columbia Capital Management of events pertaining to the Accounts and/or the City that may directly affect Columbia Capital Management's ability to manage the Accounts or perform its obligations. This one-sided structure leaves Columbia Capital Management commercially exposed, as the City may become aware of material Account-related developments — such as changes in funding, legal proceedings, or regulatory actions — and face no contractual obligation to disclose them, impairing Columbia Capital Management's investment decision-making and potentially creating liability for Columbia Capital Management for actions taken without adequate information. The absence of a reciprocal notice obligation is not commercially justified given that both parties hold information material to the Account relationship.
suggestions.original_text: Notice of Events. Consultant shall provide written notice to the City regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or Consultant. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized party of Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Notice of Events.
