Consultant shall provide written notice to the City, and the City shall provide written notice to Consultant, regarding certain events pertaining to the Accounts and/or the notifying party. Such notice shall include, at a minimum, the date, identification and description of the event triggering the notice requirement and shall be signed by an authorized party of the notifying party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains a grammatical defect — "immediately up the occurrence" — that renders the operative obligation unintelligible; no court could determine what the provision requires without resort to extrinsic evidence, leaving Columbia Capital Management unable to rely on or enforce the notice obligation. Even if the drafting error were corrected to read "immediately upon," the standard "immediately" is a vague temporal trigger that exposes Columbia Capital Management to disputes over whether any notice given was sufficiently prompt, potentially forfeiting rights that depend on timely notification. A definite, objective number of Business Days is required to give the provision enforceability and to protect Columbia Capital Management's ability to demonstrate compliance.
suggestions.original_text: Written notice shall be immediately up the occurrence of any of the following events:
suggestions.suggested_fix: Written notice shall be provided within [__] Business Days following the occurrence of any of the following events:

suggestions.reason: The phrase "material adverse change to Consultant's financial condition or status" is undefined and applies no objective threshold, leaving Consultant with broad discretion to characterise—or dismiss—deteriorating financial circumstances without triggering the notice obligation. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates a material operational risk: if Consultant experiences insolvency proceedings, a significant loss of capital, or an inability to fund ongoing performance, Columbia Capital Management may receive no advance warning and could suffer unrecoverable financial and reputational harm before it can engage a replacement service provider. Without an anchored standard, any dispute over whether notice was required would be resolved against Columbia Capital Management's interests, as Consultant controls the characterisation. This provision should therefore be tethered to objectively identifiable financial events to give Columbia Capital Management a reliably enforceable notification right.
suggestions.original_text: A material adverse change to Consultant’s financial condition or status;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Any material adverse change to Consultant's financial condition or status, including the commencement of insolvency, bankruptcy, receivership, or dissolution proceedings, or any material reduction in Consultant's ability to fund or perform its obligations under this Agreement;

suggestions.reason: The term "Custodian" is used without definition anywhere in this clause, leaving open the possibility of a dispute as to which entity the City must direct, which could expose Columbia Capital Management to residual liability claims if proxy votes are cast incorrectly or not at all. The exculpation in favor of Columbia Capital Management — "no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies" — is ambiguous in scope, and a court or counterparty could argue it covers only the act of casting a vote but not advisory or administrative activities surrounding proxy decisions, undermining the protection Columbia Capital Management intends to rely on. By defining "Custodian" within the clause and strengthening the exculpatory language to expressly include liability, Columbia Capital Management's position is materially more defensible.
suggestions.original_text: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the custodian appointed by the City to hold the City's investment assets (the "Custodian") in the voting of all proxies, and Consultant shall have no responsibility or liability in respect of the voting of proxies.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, this clause exposes Columbia Capital Management (the City) to material legal and financial risk on four fronts: it sets no professional performance standard against which the Consultant's Services can be measured, its compliance warranty is limited solely to investment adviser registration under the Consultants Act and does not extend to other applicable laws governing the engagement, it contains no warranty that the Services will be free of third-party intellectual property infringement, and it provides no remedy if any representation or warranty is breached. Without a performance standard and an infringement warranty, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual basis to demand re-performance or recover fees if the Services are deficient or give rise to a third-party claim, leaving the City bearing risks that are properly allocated to the Consultant. These gaps should also be reviewed against the Agreement's indemnification and limitation of liability provisions to confirm that warranty remedies interact consistently with the broader liability framework.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act") and shall perform the Services with the professional skill and care of an experienced investment adviser in compliance with all applicable laws; (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; and (iv) warrants that the Services will not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights, and upon breach of any warranty in this Section, shall promptly re-perform the affected Services at no additional cost to the City or, at the City's election, refund the fees paid for such Services;

suggestions.reason: The provision recites only the Consultant's authority to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement, while omitting any equivalent representation by Columbia Capital Management. This asymmetry creates an enforcement risk for Columbia Capital Management: in any dispute, a counterparty could challenge the Agreement's validity or Columbia Capital Management's standing to enforce its rights on the basis that no mutual authority representation was made. Market-standard professional services agreements require both parties to warrant their respective authority, ensuring neither party can later contest the binding effect of the Agreement against the other.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents that it is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
